method: Static reverse engineering only: atomscan, cleave facts (including decoded strings), Rizin call paths, and independently implemented decoding/decryption. No sample execution.

evidence: The root manifest is a placeholder stub with no event-bus implementation. binding.gyp uses a sources command substitution to run node index.js with stdout/stderr discarded, then echo a fake C source filename.

index.js reconstructs a decimal character array, shifts letters by one, then evals the result. The recovered stage initializes AES-128-GCM with embedded key/nonce material. One inline ciphertext produces a Bun acquisition helper; the tag-prefixed lib_native.dat sidecar decrypts and Brotli-decompresses to 1127258 bytes of JavaScript.

The loader writes that JavaScript to a randomized temporary directory, launches it through Bun, waits for exit, and removes the staged file/directory. The bootstrap resolves an installed Bun or downloads its platform ZIP with curl and extracts it; this is runtime acquisition, not proof that the Bun dependency is malicious.

Static deobfuscation of the second stage resolves a rotated custom-Base64 string array (4004 entries; rotation 123; 15445 constant decoder calls). A further PBKDF2/SHA256-derived three-round shuffled-byte decoder recovers 873 string calls. Embedded AES-256-GCM plus gzip bodies are decoded separately, without evaluating JavaScript.

T5 calls up, then cd. cd invokes filesystem, shell, GitHub runner and GitLab runner collectors. The filesystem collector enumerates secret-oriented glob paths and reads their contents. The shell collector obtains gh auth token and the entire process environment. Runner collectors locate worker processes and invoke a Python /proc/PID/maps and /proc/PID/mem reader through sudo.

ld prepares cloud secret collectors, including AWS Secrets Manager GetSecretValue, Azure Key Vault, GCP credentials and Vault token/secret access. The collectors stream successful results to ei.ingest and ei.flush; ha.dispatch passes batches to mr.createEnvelope, which compresses and AES-GCM-encrypts JSON and RSA-OAEP-wraps the key. Ei.send POSTs the envelope to an external domain; GitHub and GitLab repository senders provide fallbacks.
The recovered initial external domain is aiarmor.website with /v1/api. It is configuration evidence, not an observed connection and not a required detection token.

GitHubSender.augmentEnvelope can install a token monitor through $c, handing it rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents. The embedded monitor persists through launchd or a user service and evaluates that handler after the GitHub token receives 401/403. This is conditional destruction, not ordinary temporary-file cleanup.

Additional retained paths modify package/repository content, publish modified packages, insert CI secret-export jobs, create folder-open or agent-session hooks, and install a GitHub-commit-polled Python downloader. The placeholder packaging conceals these functions; an authorized benign event-bus purpose does not explain them.
limitations: No malicious code was executed and no live credentials or attacker service were used. Reachability is established statically; network and installation success were not tested.

Automatic analysis reconstructs the first JavaScript layer but does not decrypt the AES sidecar. The raw archive retains hostile dropper/install coverage; its inner credential theft, propagation, persistence and destructive paths still require manual decoding. No ciphertext-specific or campaign-domain YAML matcher was added.

samples.identity: Configured x86 Cobalt Strike DNS Beacon reflective DLL
evidence: The MZRE x86 bootstrap calls the exported _ReflectiveLoader@4 at VA 0x1000a036. The loader discovers its image, obtains allocation/loading APIs, copies headers/sections, resolves imports and relocations, sets protections, and invokes the mapped entry point.

The DNS loop at 0x1000440d calls 0x10002f37 for check-in data, byte-swaps/XORs the response, masks the F0 control word, and selects A/TXT/AAAA retrieval paths by flags. Received data passes through 0x1000b43b into the framed command parser at 0x10009ae2 and 117-case task dispatcher at 0x10009446.

Task 1 reaches 0x10005bed and its process-launch wrapper at 0x1000c1b4. Other dispatcher branches process file operations. Outbound data is encoded into numbered hexadecimal DNS labels at 0x100024a4. The wrapper 0x10002e92 calls the imported DnsQuery_A; this is an execution path, not an isolated DNS string.

An independent XOR-TLV parse at file offset 0x33a20 with key 0x2e yields 57 settings: DNS mode, port 53, sleep 10000ms, an RSA public key, ns1.blueorbits.site and DNS prefixes. Alternate process paths include wmiprvse.exe and msedge.exe. No configured endpoint was contacted.

At 0x1000a5b2 the loader derives NT headers from base+e_lfanew and zeros the NT signature, DOS magic and e_lfanew. A second copy of the same routine exists. Existing hostile family and DNS tasking traits and suspicious erasure/relocation observations are supported.
limitations: Cobalt Strike can be used in authorized security assessments. No such deployment context was supplied. The reusable remote-task surface, covert DNS transport and header-erasing reflective loading tip this machine-triage judgment toward MALICIOUS. The finding does not establish an operator identity or actual execution.

samples.identity: x86 Cobalt Strike DNS Beacon reflective DLL, restored headers
evidence: The MZRE bootstrap and _ReflectiveLoader@4 export at 0x10008b2d retain the same manual image-mapping/import-resolution/relocation/entry-invocation architecture.

The DNS task loop at 0x10003498 uses response-driven F0 flag checks and selects task retrieval before decoding and dispatch. DnsQuery_A and the numbered hexadecimal frame templates are used by the retained transport code.

At 0x1000907b the compiler uses ECX/EDX/EAX instead of the first DLL register ordering, but performs the same linked writes: clear NT signature, DOS magic and e_lfanew. A second copy of this variant exists. The old erasure matcher missed both; the updated matcher retains the old sequence and adds this complete variant.

The loader image-search routine at 0x10008d6d expects an NT signature value of 0x4153, whereas the supplied restored header carries PE. This can prevent the reflective search from succeeding as supplied. Retained hostile tasking and loader behavior does not require observed runtime success.
No standard XOR-TLV configuration was recovered from this file. A large zero region alone is not enough to identify the missing settings; no endpoint or successful deployment is inferred.
limitations: Cobalt Strike can be used in authorized security assessments. No such deployment context was supplied. The reusable remote-task surface, covert DNS transport and header-erasing reflective loading tip this machine-triage judgment toward MALICIOUS. The finding does not establish an operator identity or actual execution.

corrections.change: Hostile to notable, preserving every matcher leg. A data-only record decoder matches the old rule. It requires no file read, sidecar, eval, package boundary, execution sink or small size.
Notable preserved. The matcher observes an update call with Buffer.from(...,hex), not an AST condition or a proven decipher receiver.
Notable and matcher preserved. setAuthTag from a slice is an AEAD decryption operation, including ChaCha20-Poly1305; it proves neither AES nor GCM.

Hostile to notable. A normal native source generator suppressing diagnostics and echoing its output filename matches. Source-command and redirection atoms retain their complete matchers and notable level in this neutral shell-command home.

Hostile to suspicious; all required matcher legs preserved. The 8094-byte harmless packed arithmetic control matches outside test directories. Packing/character transforms establish concealment without establishing malware, a package boundary, or a megabyte minimum.

Unchanged measured predicates; static text shape moved to metadata. A single long-line outlier need not mean the entire source is one line. The complete compact profile is notable; the broad OR of numeric/long-line indications retains component criticality.
Hostile and full evidence preserved; native-build command substitution paired with a concealed packed entry is hidden-package-content behavior rather than a generic lifecycle observation.
Notable and full text matcher preserved. A textual Bun.spawn member reference establishes no shell or bridge, and does not require a call. The actual Bun.spawn call observation remains independent.

Match a Brotli API call through arbitrary receiver names, including the actual _zl.brotliDecompressSync call. Existing staged-code and ordinary decompressor fixtures retain detection; comment-only or quoted API mentions no longer assert decompression.
Preserve the original complete byte sequence and add the second complete compiler/register variant. Removing any one of the three linked writes from both routine copies defeats recognition.

consumer_audit.exact: Updated all explicit references to moved IDs, retaining the all/any sets and file/archive scopes. The encrypted-stage, crypto-decryptor, gyp sidecar, Python escape, encrypted-framing and Bun runtime composites retain their supported evidence.
consumer_audit.ancestors: Inspected exact references to every source/destination ancestor. Broad hidden-payload/install-hook selectors no longer receive ordinary crypto or build-command evidence; they retain the hostile packed-build-hook observation under hidden-payload/native-extension. consumer_audit.legacy_hold: metadata/file/data-blob::near-maximum-entropy-file remains unchanged: its source explicitly records validator admission pinned to that legacy filename for its broad archive types. Its description and matcher accurately state whole-file entropy; no attack claim is inferred.

material_detection_losses: Three overbroad hostile labels are corrected while their supported observations remain as notable or suspicious traits. The real npm sample retains three hostile behaviors in distinct leaves; neither DLL loses any attack detection. A redundant low-tier compression-library group is absent from the rendered npm parent after a concrete decompression operation is recognized; the zlib reference and new Brotli operation remain. No supported attack coverage is removed.

dependency_review.behavior: The npm postinstall determines OS/architecture/libc, resolves the appropriate @oven runtime, invokes --version, optionally installs/fetches the versioned package, unpacks it with path traversal checks, chmods the executable, then renames/links the launchers. These are expected runtime-installation functions. An error includes official manual-install instructions; printing those commands is not executing them.
dependency_review.isolation: Independent before, after and final atomscan purl runs contain no hostile or suspicious findings. The classifier probability remains 0.8399776 at level -1; no trait/classifier verdict disagreement requiring a package exception was found. Native fetched-child availability varies by run; no traits in those native artifacts were weakened.
dependency_review.edits: No dependency-specific exception or suppression was added.

remaining_disagreements: All three primary samples remain ML-hostile, matching the manual verdicts. The manually decrypted npm stage exposes theft, propagation, persistence and conditional destruction beyond the scanner automatic decoding boundary; that automatic behavior-coverage gap remains.

validation_controls.cases: Benign AEAD records, ChaCha tag slices, native source generation, harmless packing, real Brotli calls versus mentions, three existing fixtures outside this batch, actual packed and decoded npm stages, archive scope, both original PE erasure variants and six missing-write mutations.
validation_controls.debug_layer_scope: test-rules evaluates call symbols at its exact target, so process sinks are checked on independently recovered first-layer source. Normal atomscan retains and reports decoded-member findings.
